human_tolerance.notes: Successful in dry secondary forests and edge habitats; introduced populations live within the cities of Rio de Janeiro and Buenos Aires, so the species copes well with disturbed and urbanised land.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Breeding is not strongly seasonal: gestation lasts about five months and females are ready to breed again about ten days after giving birth, so a group can produce two litters a year.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Infants cling to the mother's back for the first two weeks, are weaned at three months, enter the juvenile stage at five months and reach adult size at 15 months.

vocalizations.description: A series of short, repeating calls that rise in pitch with each note; given at a threat.
Short, trickling, high-pitched calls given alone or in a series; alarm calls that elicit fleeing from other group members.
Vibrato-like, low-pitched generic calls used to monitor and locate group members.
Whistle-like, high-pitched generic calls given in series of one to five notes; attract mates, keep the group together, defend territories and locate missing members.

external.note: GBIF usage key 5219542 and iNaturalist taxon id 43373 as given in issue #25; ITIS TSN 572915 and NCBI taxon id 9483 via Wikidata (P815, P685).

common_names.note: English and German names from Wikidata (P1843); Portuguese 'sagui-de-tufo-branco' from the article's interlanguage links.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005); the article's taxobox shows IUCN 3.1 Least Concern.

range.note: Native to northeastern Brazil (Piauí, Paraíba, Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, Pernambuco, Alagoas, Bahia); introduced to Southeast Brazil since the 1920s, where it is invasive (recorded in Rio de Janeiro from 1929), and to Buenos Aires, Argentina. invasive_in lists BR for the introduced Southeast Brazilian population, which lies inside the native country.

traits.body_plan.note: Quadrupedal primate; the issue and recipe specify quadruped, matching the small arboreal quadruped template.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Runs across branches quadrupedally, clings vertically to tree trunks and leaps between trees; Walk and Climb chosen. Climb has no pose in body-plans.json, so no climb pose is declared.

traits.nest_type.note: Judgement: marmosets do not build a nest; they sleep in dense vine tangles and isolated tree canopies, so None is the honest value. The article does not describe a nest.

traits.perching.note: Sits and sleeps on branches but does not perch like a bird; set to false, as for the grey squirrel.

traits.mass_kg.note: Mean of EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 292 g and PanTHERIA AdultBodyMass_g 290.21 g. Wikipedia gives lower sex averages (males 256 g, females 236 g) and the Handbook of the Mammals of the World means of 317-322 g; the two trait datasets agree with each other and sit between them.

traits.length_m.note: Head-body length 0.187 m (Wikipedia: males 188 mm, females 185 mm) plus a long tail of roughly 0.19 m, consistent with the judgement tail_ratio of 1.2; the article describes the tail as relatively long and banded but gives no measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia's marmoset article states 'they can live up to 14 years old in the wild'; PanTHERIA MaxLongevity is 201.6 months (16.8 y), a captivity maximum. 12 years used as a typical wild lifespan between the two.

traits.home_range_ha.note: PanTHERIA HomeRange_km2 0.02 km2 converted to hectares; consistent with the 2-5 ha group home ranges described in the Handbook of the Mammals of the World.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits records Diet-Nect 40, Diet-Fruit 30, Diet-Inv 20, Diet-Vunk 10; Wikipedia describes a diet primarily of plant exudates (20-70% of feeding behaviour) and insects (24-30% of food), with fruit, seeds, flowers, fungi, nectar, snails, lizards, frogs, eggs and nestlings also taken. The split follows the coordinator's recipe (fruit 0.4, invertebrate 0.3, browse 0.2, nectar 0.1), mapping exudates to browse; it is a judgement reconciling the two sources, not a direct reading of either.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: stable extended families of up to 15 members, typically nine, with one or two breeding females, a breeding male, their offspring and adult relatives; PanTHERIA SocialGrpSize 8.55 agrees. Group structure with group_size [3, 15] per the recipe, 3 being a conservative minimum for a breeding pair with offspring.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Activity-Diurnal 1 (exclusively diurnal); the article describes a diurnal species active between sunrise and the late afternoon.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: a small arboreal primate that retreats into dense canopy when threatened. The article describes alarm calls (staccatos, tsiks) given in threatening situations but does not detail the escape response.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: introduced populations live in cities (Rio de Janeiro, Buenos Aires) and are bold around people; wild groups are warier. 0.4, slightly below the grey squirrel's 0.45 for a smaller, more vulnerable animal.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value 'Ar' (arboreal) gives the primary stratum; the ground share is judgement, reflecting the species' almost entirely arboreal life in the understory and canopy.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Judgement: sleeps in dense, vine-covered vegetation and isolated tree canopies rather than tree cavities or a built nest, so shrub_thicket is the closest tag. The article does not describe sleeping sites.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the shrub_thicket shelter weight is judgement since no open source gives its relative importance.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: The article describes success in dry secondary forests and edge habitats and introduced populations living within the cities of Rio de Janeiro and Buenos Aires.

habitat.density_per_ha.note: Typical from PanTHERIA PopulationDensity_n/km2 508.18 converted to per-hectare; min and max are an authored tenfold band either side, following the same convention used for sciurus-carolinensis.

seasonal.strategy.note: Tropical species active year round; no dormancy or migration described.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding is not strongly seasonal (females can give birth twice a year), so the mating and young phases span the whole year; gestation, weaning and growth timings from the Reproduction and parenting section.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration from 'at 15 months, they reach adult size' (450 days used); scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: Descriptions and contexts (staccato and tsik alarm calls, trill and phee contact calls) from the article's Communication section; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement since no open source quantifies them. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

look.note: Colours from the article's description (marbled brown, grey and yellow pelage, white ear tufts, banded tail, black nose skin, white forehead blaze); proportions follow the sciurus-carolinensis template with tail_ratio 1.2 (judgement for a long, non-prehensile tail); the ear-tuft and forehead-blaze extra parts are authored to render the species' distinctive white markings.

behavior.note: Authored program (species/callithrix-jacchus/behavior.json) modelling the daily cycle the article describes: feed on fruit or gum at dawn, forage for insects, rest and groom through the midday, retire at dusk. States forage -> social_groom -> sentinel -> rest, with wander and flee scaffolding; the social_groom transition requires nearby group members (conspecifics_within_m) to express the troop life the shared ground-forager program does not model. rest_sun_lo_deg/rest_sun_hi_deg set to -90/-6 per the program's description for a diurnal species (rests while the sun is below the horizon).
